newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Syria making more lethal nerve gas.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Syria making more lethal nerve gas.

text.p: Israel said on Tuesday Syria was making a more lethal nerve gas and warned Damascus the Jewish state had means many times more destructive at its disposal.
"We discovered it a few months ago," Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told reporters.
He was commenting on a report by the Israeli newspaper Haaretz that Syria was manufacturing a nerve gas called VX that acts via the skin and is hard to disperse.

"I discussed it with U.S. Defence Secretary (William) Cohen during my last visit to the United States. I discussed it with the government of the United Kingdom and I think all the Western countries know what Syria is producing," Mordechai said.

Haaretz's respected military analyst Zeev Schiff, quoting Western intelligence sources, said Syria also was in the initial stages of preparing warheads for ground-to-ground missiles that could deliver the gas.
The Syrians already have Sarin gas which acts via the respiratory system, Schiff wrote. "But this time they've entered a new area, a new gas named VX," he told Israel Radio.
Foreign Minister David Levy, asked about the reported manufacture of VX, said: "Anyone who does this understands also that we have possibilities over and above what the other side can imagine."
Levy told the radio that Israel would continue with "the vital things that we are also developing...for the purpose of deterence".
The "other side", he said, must understand that "it alone does not control something serious like this but that we also control things that are seven times more serious".
Both Mordechai and Levy called on Syria to return to peace talks which ground to a halt at the beginning of 1996 under Israel's previous Labour-led government.

In May, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the right-wing Likud party was elected after a campaign in which he insisted Israel must keep the Golan Heights it captured from Syria in 1967. Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal.

"We are looking forward to achieving peace, a real peace...but at the same time we know that we are strong enough against any threat in the Middle East. We don't want any war, any battle," Mordechai said.
Israel has declined comment over the years on news reports in France and elsewhere that a facility in a suburb of Tel Aviv is working on biological and chemical weapons.

Also according to foreign news reports, Israel has a nuclear arsenal of at least 200 bombs. Israel's only comment on the nuclear option is that it will not be the first to introduce nuclear weapons to the Middle East.
